newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians call for NATO protest on Victory Day.
newsitem.headline: Russians call for NATO protest on Victory Day.

text.p: Russia's lower house of parliament on Thursday urged Russians to take to the streets on May 9, a holiday celebrating the end of World War Two, to protest against NATO plans to expand into eastern Europe.

The communist-dominated State Duma, in an appeal to citizens passed by a vote of 253 for and 14 against, said NATO's expected plans to invite former Warsaw Pact states to join the alliance posed a grave threat to Moscow.
"Today, external dangers for our nation are beginning to increase," the resolution said.

"Plans to expand the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, underneath all the verbal camouflage they have hidden, means one thing: moving the NATO military machine towards the borders of Russia and the emergence of the greatest military threat to our country for the past half century."
The appeal calls for political parties, public organisations and other groups to take part in the May 9 Victory Day protest.

President Boris Yeltsin has often strongly criticised NATO expansion plans, but has also said Moscow is ready to sign a charter agreement on relations between Russia and the alliance on May 27 in Paris.
Victory Day, marking the victory over Nazi Germany in World War Two, has been celebrated with increased pomp since other Soviet-era anniversaries were dropped or downgraded.
That victory enabled Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin to set up loyal communist regimes across Eastern Europe, creating a security buffer against potential Western aggression during the Cold War.
